# Configuration keys

Source: `config/harness-knobs.json`.

Use `provenant config schema` for effective values, or `provenant config schema --all` for all editable fields and their effective values; the [advanced reference](config-keys-all.md) documents host policy and tuning.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `profile` | balanced | Select balanced or economy defaults |
| `lanes.max_concurrency` | 8 | Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when any lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins. |
| `lanes.max_concurrency_read_only` | 16 | Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when no lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. A lanes.max_concurrency you set yourself also caps it unless you set this knob too. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins. |
| `lanes.max_depth` | 2 | Maximum nested lane depth, including the first dispatched lane. |
| `lanes.silence_seconds` | 1800 | Mark a provider observation silent after this many seconds without output or CPU progress; never kill it for silence. |
| `lanes.slot_wait_seconds` | 7200 | Most time in total that a lane's build-slot waits keep off its wall-clock deadline. Beyond it the wall deadline runs while the lane waits, so a stuck lane cannot wait forever. 0 keeps no waiting off the deadline. |
| `lanes.publish` | False | Opt-in. Let worktree-write lanes with open network read gh configuration, use a git credential helper, push branches and open pull requests. |
| `routing.exclude` | [] | Keep each listed provider (claude), account (label, entry or adapter/key) or exact model (adapter/id) out of named-route pools for every task. A standing list; `--exclude` and a graph's list are added to it, not substituted for it. A pinned `--model` is never affected. |
| `routing.graph_exclude` | [] | The exclusion list a graph passes to each node it launches, set from graph routing policy. Same selectors as `routing.exclude`; refusals and `--explain` name the graph as the source. |
| `fabric.accept_handoff` | False | Let a Fabric peer start a Claude session on this host through a session hand-off. |
| `usage.project_attribution` | False | Include the existing project identifier in local usage events. |
| `domains.run.writer_token_budget` | 500000 | Tokens a writer attempt may use, from the fresh usage its provider reports, before it is ended so a continuation can pick it up. The host then attempts to commit and publish the lane's work; it does not when custody is not absent, when a merge, cherry-pick, revert or rebase is in progress, or when the commit fails, and settlement notes say which. 0 turns the budget off. Cache reads do not count. Enforced for Claude from live usage. The budget does not stop Codex writers: codex exec reports usage only at its final turn.completed frame, with no further turn to stop. Other providers without live usage are also not enforced. Launch warnings or receipt notes say so. Current lane adapters cannot receive a live steer: the 90% warning records an unsupported control receipt. After custody is absent the host attempts a bounded commit; an in-progress merge is preserved for stopped-merge handling, a cherry-pick, revert or rebase in progress is left uncommitted, and a skipped or failed commit is reported without replacing the budget outcome. Time queued for a build slot does not count towards the wall-clock deadline, up to lanes.slot_wait_seconds in total. The source (run, project, host or default) is shown with the budget. |
| `domains.pr.land.integration` | batch | Integration strategy. |
| `domains.pr.land.batch_size` | 8 | Maximum pull requests in a batch. |
| `domains.pr.land.gate.checks` | ci-status | Required candidate checks. |
| `domains.pr.land.gate.timeout_seconds` | 3600 | Candidate gate timeout. |
| `domains.pr.land.local_gate.mode` | warn | Fast pre-push gate behaviour. |
| `domains.pr.land.local_gate.commands` | empty | Fast pre-push command plan. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.nodes` | 512 | Graph nodes limit. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.expansion_depth` | 64 | Longest dependency chain in edges, root nodes at depth 0, and deepest composite nesting a graph may expand to. Graph documents cannot raise it. |
| `domains.fabric.graph.limits.concurrency` | 0 | Graph concurrency limit. Zero uses host lane caps. |
| `domains.fabric.lanes.max_concurrent_builds` | max(1, min(cores / cargo_build_jobs, GiB of RAM / 6)) | A build throttle, not a hard cap: cargo builds, tests, checks and lints that a lane's cargo shim runs at once across the host and every project that shares the state directory. Lanes are not capped by it; a command that compiles waits for a free slot. Direct ~/.cargo/bin/cargo, rustc and non-cargo builds are not gated. |
| `domains.fabric.lanes.build_wait_minutes` | 30 | Minutes a build waits for a build slot or another build's Cargo lock before it gives up with an error. |
| `providers.{provider}.update` | True | Run the detected native updater in a detached one-shot worker scheduled by quota events. Provider preparation briefly shares the update lock; running lanes do not hold it. If all candidates are updating, dispatch waits at most --wait (capped at 30 seconds), then uses the installed version. false opts out; {command: [program, argument, ...]} overrides the updater directly without a shell. |
| `providers.{provider}.runtime_deadline_seconds` | unset | Cap on the wall-clock runtime of any lane on this provider. A dispatch's own --provider-timeout applies when it is shorter. At the deadline the provider is stopped and the attempt settles as timed_out, whatever the host did meanwhile, including sleeping. |
| `gc.graph_checkpoint_days` | 90 | Retain terminal graph checkpoints for at least this many days after their last save |
